State Volleyball Runner-Up (2022)\u003C/li>\n\u003C/ul>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Junior (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>One of the Big Ten's most consistent long-range shooters, Logan Nissley returns for her third season as a Husker ready to help lead an experienced Big Red backcourt.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 28 games, Nissley has averaged 8.9 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists despite being limited by minor injuries. She also has moved to No. 6 on Nebraska's career three-point list with 174 made.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley pumped in a career-high 22 points on a career-best 6-of-12 three-point shooting against No. 22 Maryland (Feb. 7). Her previous season high came with 15 points to go with three assists in a Big Ten win over Illinois (Jan. 24), before adding 14 points, on 4-of-6 three-point shooting in a win over Northwestern (Jan. 28). She added a season-best five rebounds against the Wildcats.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley added 15 points, five rebounds and five assists in a gutsy effort while battling illness at Oregon (Feb. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She pitched in 14 points on 4-of-6 shooting in NU's 101-83 win at Penn State (Dec. 6). Nissley drained three three-pointers in a 2:30 span in the fourth quarter to help NU pull away down the stretch with the highest scoring period (36) in school history.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley, who owns 13 double-figure scoring efforts on the year, put up 12 points and four rebounds against Indiana in the Big Ten Tournament (March 4). She also had 12 points and four assists at Minnesota (Feb. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She contributed 11 points - all in the fourth quarter with three threes - to help Nebraska pull away in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24). She followed with four assists in an Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship game win over Virginia (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 11 points at No. 11 Ohio State (Feb. 1). Nissley had 11 points against No. 4 UCLA when she went 3-for-5 from long range. She also had 11 points in a Big Ten win over Indiana (Jan. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored 10 points in a season-high 29 minutes against No. 17 USC (Dec. 29). She had 10 points, five boards and a career-high seven assists in a win over Bradley (Dec. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley contributed eight points and a pair of threes in a Big Ten road win at Washington (Feb. 22). She opened the season with eight points, three rebounds and two assists off the bench in a 103-46 win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3). She added eight points and two steals in an 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had eight more to go with five rebounds, two steals and her second block of the year in an 87-56 win over Cal Baptist (Dec. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She did not play in Nebraska's wins over Samford (Nov. 8) and Creighton (Nov. 12) because of a lower leg injury. She returned with three points, two rebounds and an assist in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16), before getting seven points, two rebounds and three assists in less than 14 minutes in a 103-58 win over Oral Roberts (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Last year, Nissley was a primary starter in the Husker backcourt despite being limited by foot injuries. She averaged 7.0 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.6 assists. While her scoring and rebounding numbers were similar to her freshman season, Nissley more than doubled her production in assists, steals and blocks.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Her all-around play and high basketball IQ make her a versatile weapon in the NU arsenal.\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>A member of the Big Ten All-Freshman Team by both the coaches and the media in 2024, Nissley was a regular starter in the Nebraska backcourt as a sophomore in 2024-25. The 6-0 guard from Bismarck, N.D., averaged 7.0 points, 2.7 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.1 steals over 32 games with 26 starts.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley closed the season with nine points on a trio of three-pointers to go with three assists and two steals against Louisville in the NCAA Tournament (March 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 7.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.0 steals in the Big Ten Tournament, scoring eight points and tying a career high with seven rebounds in a win over Illinois (March 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced her eighth double-figure scoring effort with a season-high 16 points on a career-high five threes in a win over Oregon (Feb. 19). She also tied a career high with seven boards against the Ducks, while adding a season-high five assists to go with two steals.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley had 11 points, five rebounds and a season-high-tying five assists in NU's upset at No. 17 Maryland (Feb. 13). It followed an 11-point, five-assist showing against Iowa (Feb. 10). She also had 13 points and five assists in a win at Iowa (Jan. 16). She scored 10 points in the final 11 minutes to help NU rally from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. Nissley had 14 points on 4-of-5 three-point shooting at No. 4 USC (Jan. 1). She had 11 points on three threes at No. 17 Georgia Tech (Dec. 21). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored in double figures off the bench in each of Nebraska’s first two games of 2024-25, including 14 points to go with four assists in a win over Southeastern Louisiana (Nov. 9). She also hit four threes against the Lady Lions.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened with 12 points and three assists in just 11 minutes in a win over Omaha (Nov. 4). She went a career-best 5-for-5 at the free throw line against the Mavs.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley made her first start of the year in the record-setting win over South Dakota (Nov. 16), knocking down a trio of threes to finish with nine points. She added nine points and three boards in a win over Lindenwood (Dec. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2023-24)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Nissley increased her production throughout the season and joined Nebraska’s starting lineup down the stretch as a freshman. She played in all 35 games for the Huskers, including 10 starts to end the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 7.0 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists while sinking the second-most three-pointers by a freshman (59) in Nebraska history. The only Husker to hit more threes as a freshman than Nissley was first-team All-American and 2014 Big Ten Player of the Year Jordan Hooper with 67 in 2010-11.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley played a major role in Nebraska's first-round NCAA Tournament win over Texas A&M by matching Alexis Markowski with a team-high 16 points. Nissley buried 4-of-6 threes against the Aggies, while adding three rebounds and two steals in the 61-59 victory. Her two free throws with 17 seconds left gave the Huskers a 60-59 lead.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Her four threes against Texas A&M tied her season high for the fifth time, including a 4-for-10 effort from long range in the Big Ten Championship Game against No. 3 Iowa, when she finished with 13 points and five assists in a season-high 34 minutes. She also went 4-for-6 from long range on her way to 12 points and a career-high six assists in a win over Northwestern (Feb. 20), after going 4-for-5 from beyond the arc in a win over Southern (Dec. 17). Nissley established her season best by hitting 4-of-6 threes on her way to a career-high 18 points in a win over UNCW (Dec. 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The three-time North Dakota Gatorade High School Player of the Year matched her career scoring high with 18 points in a road win at Purdue (Feb. 17) in her first career start. Nissley helped Nebraska rally from a 10-point first-quarter deficit by scoring 11 first-half points and NU’s first six points of the second half.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley averaged 9.2 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.9 assists while hitting 42.9 percent (21-49) of her three-pointers in 10 games as a starter.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also erupted for one of her best efforts of the season with 15 points and a career-high seven rebounds in 24 minutes in Nebraska’s 82-79 upset of No. 2 Iowa (Feb. 11), just two games prior to making her starting debut.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley produced 12 double-figure scoring efforts on the season, including 11 points - all in the third quarter - of Nebraska’s 73-61 Big Ten quarterfinal win over Michigan State (March 8). She notched six double-figure efforts in the final 12 games beginning with her 12-point performance in the win over No. 2 Iowa (Feb. 11).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley notched her first double-figure effort with 10 points in a win over Alcorn State (Nov. 14). She added 11 points in 12 minutes against TCU (Nov. 25), before pumping in 11 points in 13 minutes in a win over Georgia Tech (Dec. 2). Nissley hit three threes against the Yellow Jackets, including back-to-back fourth-quarter threes to turn a two-point NU deficit into a four-point lead the Huskers never relinquished. She added 13 points on 3-of-6 three-point shooting against No. 14 Indiana (Jan. 7).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>A three-time North Dakota basketball state player of the year, Nissley averaged 20.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 3.9 steals as a senior in 2022-23. She helped the Patriots to a state runner-up finish for the second straight year, while closing her career with 1,664 points.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley was ranked as the No. 91 player in the Class of 2023 by ESPN after averaging more than 21 points and three steals while hitting 47 percent of her three-pointers as a junior in 2021-22. She led Bismarck Century to a 50-game winning streak over two seasons before claiming a state runner-up finish in 2022. In the 2022 Class A state championship game, Nissley put up 32 points, 11 rebounds and four assists.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a sophomore in 2020-21, Nissley powered Bismarck Century to a state title to win Gatorade and MaxPreps North Dakota Player of the Year honors after producing school records with 556 points (21.4 ppg), 100 assists and 93 steals while hitting 46.4 percent of her three-point attempts. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A four-time volleyball letterwinner, Nissley captured back-to-back North Dakota Volleyball Player of the Year awards in 2021 and 2022. She finished her career with more than 1,000 career kills and 1,000 career digs. As a senior, she recorded 361 digs, 357 kills, 34 blocks and 19 service aces while leading the Patriots to their second straight volleyball state championship. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nissley played her club basketball for North Tartan - the same program as former Huskers Sam Haiby and Annika Stewart.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>The daughter of Brad and Ashley Nissley, Logan was born in Bismarck, N.D. She has a younger brother, Garrett. A child, youth and family studies major, Logan was an Academic All-District VII selection by the College Sports Communicators in 2025. She was also a Big Ten Distinguished Scholar and an Academic All-Big Ten choice following her sophomore season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A four-time Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll selection, Nissley was also a member of the Tom Osborne Citizenship Team in 2024 and 2025. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She selected Nebraska over Gonzaga, Minnesota, Utah and Iowa.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"I chose Nebraska because of the family culture the girls brought to me when I visited,\" Nissley said. \"The program itself and the facilities are amazing, but it felt like my second home and I knew it was meant for me. The coaches were unmatched and were by far my favorite because they cared about me as a person not just an athlete.\"\u003C/div>\n\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Logan Nissley's Career 2021)\u003C/p>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Redshirt (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Allison Weidner (pronounced WIDE-ner) returns for her fifth season as a Husker after enduring her third season-ending knee injury midway through the 2024-25 campaign. She plans to redshirt in 2025-26 in hopes of returning healthy for 2026-27 while also completing her master's degree in educational psychology.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The graduate student from the small Northeast Nebraska town of Humphrey (pop. 832) earned her bachelor's degree in child, youth and family studies in December 2024. A Big Ten Distinguished Scholar in 2025, she is a three-time Academic All-Big Ten selection.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner had outstanding rehabs on both her left and right knees heading into 2024-25, before suffering a right knee injury in practice (Jan. 11, 2025) prior to Nebraska's road game at Rutgers. She underwent surgery on Jan. 28, 2025, and has had another excellent rehab.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The 5-10 guard averaged 10.2 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists while starting Nebraska's first 13 games in 2022-23, before suffering a left ACL tear against No. 20 Kansas (Dec. 21, 2022). She was ready for the start of practice before the 2023-24 season, but suffered a right ACL tear in practice on Oct. 13, 2023.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nebraska's Lifter of the Year in 2023-24, Weidner is one of the best all-around athletes in state history as a seven-time all-state selection in basketball (4) and volleyball (3) and an eight-time state champion in track and field.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In 10 career Big Ten starts as a freshman (8) and sophomore (2), Weidner helped Nebraska to a 7-3 record including a pair of wins over top-20 teams (No. 10 Michigan, No. 20 Maryland) away from Pinnacle Bank Arena. In those 10 starts, Weidner averaged 10.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Redshirt Junior (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Weidner made her return to Nebraska’s starting lineup with 11 points in a season-opening win over Omaha (Nov. 4). Weidner, who missed nearly two years with back-to-back knee injuries, added three rebounds, two steals and an assist in a team-high 24 minutes of action against the Mavs.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She matched her season highs with 11 points and six assists off the bench in Nebraska's win over No. 20 Michigan State (Jan. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner was averaging 3.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steal over 15 games before suffering a season-ending right knee injury in practice (Jan. 11). She underwent surgery on Jan. 28.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had five points, three rebounds and two steals in a win over Chattanooga (Dec. 15). She grabbed a season-high seven rebounds in the win over Tarleton State (Dec. 11).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Medical Redshirt (2023-24)\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Weidner was on track to return to Nebraska's starting lineup as a junior in 2023-24 before suffering a right knee injury in practice on Oct. 13. She underwent surgery on Oct. 25, and was with the Huskers on the sideline while redshirting in 2023-24.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Her recovery and rehab after surgery went well on her left knee before suffering her right knee injury just three weeks before the start of the 2023-24 regular season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2022-23)\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Weidner showed major improvements to her all-around game while taking on a greater leadership role in her second season. She averaged 10.2 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists while starting each of Nebraska's first 13 games of 2022-23. She scored in double figures in four consecutive games before suffering a season-ending leg injury early in the fourth quarter of NU's triple-overtime win over No. 20 Kansas (Dec. 21). She underwent successful surgery on Jan. 10.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner had 13 points, seven rebounds and three assists in a win over Wyoming (Dec. 18). It followed her second double-double of the season with 15 points, 11 rebounds and a career-high five steals in a win over Samford (Dec. 10).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched her first career double-double with 13 points and a career-high 15 rebounds in Nebraska's upset of No. 20 Maryland in College Park (Dec. 4). Weidner, who added five assists against the Terps, scored all 13 of her points and grabbed eight of her rebounds in the second half alone, as NU outscored Maryland 59-31 in the second half. Weidner's effort helped the Huskers secure their first-ever win over Maryland, which went on to advance to the NCAA Elite Eight.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner added 13 points, five rebounds and seven assists in an 82-54 win over Wisconsin (Dec. 7) to help the Huskers improve to 2-0 in Big Ten play despite the absence of starters Isabelle Bourne, Trinity Brady and Sam Haiby - who all missed the game with injuries.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner opened the season with 19 points and a then-career-high nine rebounds in a win over Omaha (Nov. 7). She made a career-high nine field goals in just 11 attempts against the Mavs. She added her second career 20-point performance with 20 points and seven boards in a win over Houston Christian (Nov. 11).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She was injured on an offensive rebound on the first possession of the game against Tarleton (Nov. 22), but still finished the play with a bucket in the opening minute before she left the court. Weidner, who played 59 seconds, did not return to the game after suffering an eye injury. She did return to the starting lineup three days later in NU's win over Texas A&M-Corpus Christi at the Puerto Rico Clasico (Nov. 25). She had 13 points and five rebounds against the Islanders.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2021-22)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Weidner joined Alexis Markowski as freshman starters in Nebraska's lineup down the stretch in 2021-22. Weidner averaged 7.2 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.2 assists while playing in all 33 games for the 24-9 Huskers in 2021-22.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She moved into Nebraska's starting five for the final eight games of the season and started nine contests overall for the Huskers, who finished No. 23 in the NET rankings and advanced to the 2022 NCAA Tournament.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced the most memorable performance of her young career with a team-high 16 points, including two free throws with 5.5 seconds left to seal Nebraska's 76-73 victory over No. 10 Michigan in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals in Indianapolis (March 4). Weidner added three rebounds, two assists and two steals against the Wolverines to give Nebraska two wins over the eventual 2022 NCAA Elite Eight qualifiers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner put together her best game with a career-high 23 points and a career-best three threes in a 93-70 win over Minnesota (Feb. 20). She hit 8-of-10 shots from the field, including all three of her long-range attempts, while also going 4-for-4 from the free throw line against the Gophers. She added five rebounds.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored in double figures seven times on the season, including 11 points, eight rebounds and five assists in just 18 minutes off the bench in a win over Prairie View A&M (Nov. 11). She added 10 points, five boards and three assists in a victory over Drake (Dec. 19), before producing her first double-digit effort in Big Ten play with 14 points and five rebounds off the bench in a win over Purdue (Jan. 30). She scored all 14 points in the first half against the Boilermakers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner matched that performance with 14 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals in a win over Penn State (Feb. 3). She scored 10 points in the fourth quarter to help the Huskers turn a one-point lead into a 15-point win. Weidner also had 11 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal in Nebraska's 72-55 run past No. 5 Indiana (Feb. 14). She hit 5-of-7 shots from the field, including her lone three-point attempt, to help the Huskers to their largest victory margin ever against a top-five team. The win over Indiana marked Weidner's last game off the bench in 2021-22.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In nine starts on the season, Weidner averaged 9.3 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.0 assists. She made her first career start in place of an injured Sam Haiby at Iowa (Jan. 16), in a game the Huskers also played without starting guard Jaz Shelley (COVID protocols). Weidner finished with eight points, three rebounds, five assists and a block against the Hawkeyes.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner made a solid debut with nine points in a win over Maine (Nov. 9) and threatened a triple-double with eight points, eight rebounds and eight assists in just 18 minutes off the bench in a win over North Carolina Central (Nov. 20). Her eight rebounds and eight assists were both season highs.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>One of the top small-school players in Nebraska history, Weidner finished her four-year high school career with 2,282 points, 741 assists and 629 steals. Her career point total ranked No. 3 across all classes in Nebraska girls basketball history, while she became just the 13th player in state history to score 2,000 career points. The star from Humphrey St. Francis High School was a four-time first-team Class D2 All-State selection for Coach Bryan Reichmuth. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A first-team all-class, all-state pick by both the Omaha World-Herald and the Lincoln Journal Star as both a junior and senior, Weidner led the state in scoring with 25.0 points per game as a senior, while also leading the state with 6.4 assists per game. Her 6.4 steals per game also ranked second in the state across all classes, while she added 7.0 rebounds per contest. Weidner scored 71 points over three state tournament wins to lead Humphrey St. Francis to the state title.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior, Weidner averaged 25.2 points, 6.1 rebounds, 6.5 assists and a whopping 7.3 steals per game in 2020. She also led the Flyers to a state runner-up finish while earning a spot on the Class D2 All-Tournament team. She scored a state tournament-best 83 points over three games as a junior. She led St. Francis to a Class D2 state runner-up finish as a freshman and claimed her first selection to the all-tournament team. Weidner also guided the Flyers to a state tournament bid as a sophomore in 2019. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior, Weidner nearly notched a quadruple-double with 28 points, 10 assists, 10 steals and nine rebounds against Elkhorn Valley. She also produced a triple-double with 29 points, 12 rebounds and 10 steals against Fullerton. In the 2020 state tournament, she erupted for a career-high 39 points against Mullen. She had 38 points against Howells/Dodge.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also led the state in assists in both 2018 and 2019, while leading the state in steals in 2019.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner played club basketball for the Nebraska Attack and Coach Zach Isherwood. She led the Attack to the championship of the Nike Tournament of Champions Session 2, Gold Division. The Nebraska Attack also finished fifth at Under Armour Nationals and won the Midwest Basketball Showcase.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Chosen as one of the top multi-sport athletes in the state by the Lincoln Journal Star in 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21, Weidner was also a first-team all-stater in volleyball while leading St. Francis to a state runner-up finish as a junior in 2019. She was also an honorable-mention Class D2 all-state choice and led the Flyers to a third-place finish as a sophomore in 2018. She guided Humphrey St. Francis back to the state tournament as a senior in 2020.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>On the track, Weidner swept the Class D2 state titles in the 400 and 800-meter runs in 2018, 2019 and 2021. She added two more state titles as a member of the 3,200-meter relay team as a sophomore and senior, after helping the 1,600-meter relay to a state runner-up finish as a freshman. Weidner also finished sixth in the triple jump as a senior. No state track and field championships were held in 2020 because of COVID-19. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She earned 11 letters across basketball, volleyball and track at St. Francis, capturing a total of 10 individual or team state championships.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner was also a leader in the classroom at Humphrey St. Francis. She earned Academic All-State honors in basketball as a senior (winter 2021) and volleyball as a junior (fall 2019). She was a two-year member of the National Honor Society, serving as the group’s treasurer as a senior. She was also a member in the Big Sisters Program at Humphrey St. Francis.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Dan and Cathy Weidner, Allison was born in Norfolk, Neb. She has two older brothers, Brandon and Nathan. A child, youth and family studies major, Allison earned her bachelor's degree from Nebraska in December 2024. She was a 2025 Big Distinguished Scholar and a three-time Academic All-Big Ten pick. She is an eight-time Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll selection and a four-time member of the Tom Osborne Citizenship Team. She also earned a prestigious Sam Foltz 27 Hero Leadership Award in 2025. She is pursuing a master's degree in educational psychology.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner is the Big Ten Representative on the Nebraska Student-Athlete Advisory Committee in 2025-26.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weidner chose Nebraska over Creighton, South Dakota, South Dakota State, Duquesne, Omaha, Denver, Toledo, North Dakota State and Wyoming.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"I chose Nebraska because of the family atmosphere that the coaches and staff provide,\" Weidner said. “The support that Nebraska provides to its student-athletes is something that stood out to me. As a child I always dreamed of playing for Nebraska and representing my home state. It is truly an honor to be a Husker. (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Kennadi Williams is seeing her first action as a Husker women's basketball player in her second year with the program in 2025-26. The daughter of Nebraska Head Coach Amy Williams, Kennadi sat out her true freshman basketball season at Nebraska while continuing to rehabilitate a knee injury suffered following her high school basketball senior season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 30 contests, Williams is averaging 2.5 points and 2.4 assists in 15 minutes per game off the bench, while carrying a team-best 2.6-to-1 assist-to-turnover ratio.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Williams set a career high with eight points in a win over Cal Baptist (Dec. 21), after matching her then-career high with seven points in an 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced a then-season-high seven points in a 103-58 win over ORU (Nov. 19).  \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She dished out a career-high six assists with no turnovers while adding three points, a rebound and a steal in Nebraska's 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with five points, three assists and two steals in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Williams, who amassed 71 assists on the year, had five assists to go with three points and two steals at No. 11 Ohio State (Feb. 1). She also had five assists to go with two points in a win over Samford (Nov. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added four assists and two points to go with two steals in a win over North Dakota State in Sioux Falls, S.D. (Nov. 16). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Williams contributed two points, two boards and an assist while playing important minutes in support of Husker guards in early foul trouble in NU's 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Williams hit her first career three-pointer in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24), before adding two points and forcing a crucial turnover by Virginia All-American Kymora Johnson in the final minute to help the Huskers capture the Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She hit a first-half three-pointer after a steal while dishing out three assists with no turnovers in Nebraska's 101-83 win at Penn State (Dec. 6). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added a three-pointer and two assists in NU's Big Ten home win over Indiana (Jan. 8). Although Williams did not gain game experience on the court as a freshman, she did play in 44 games with one start for the Nebraska softball team in the spring of 2025, helping the Big Red to an NCAA Super Regional appearance. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>An accomplished three-sport star at Lincoln Southwest High School, Williams was the 2022 Lincoln Journal Star High School Female Athlete of the Year as a sophomore. The Southwest basketball, softball and soccer teams earned state tournament trips each of her four seasons on the teams.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"Kennadi has been passionate about this program since we came to Lincoln, and it is her dream to represent the Huskers and help push this program to national prominence,\" Williams said. \"She is a tough competitor, a gifted athlete, and an amazing teammate who will do whatever it takes to help her team win. I am really looking forward to sharing this experience with her.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Redshirt (2024-25)\u003C/strong>\u003C/div>\nWilliams took a basketball redshirt season while continuing to recover from a knee injury suffered as a high school soccer player on March 23, 2024.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Her rehabilitation allowed her to compete in 44 games with the Nebraska softball team. She scored 19 runs and went 4-for-5 on stolen base attempts to help Coach Rhonda Revelle's Huskers advance to an NCAA Super Regional.\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv> \u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>A four-year varsity letter winner in basketball, softball and soccer at Lincoln Southwest, Williams was a Class A all-state selection and a member of the Class A All-Tournament Team while leading the Silver Hawks to a runner-up finish at the Nebraska girls basketball tournament in 2022. She was also an honorable-mention all-state choice in 2023, despite missing 80 percent of the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a senior, Williams averaged team bests of 16.5 points, 3.2 assists and 3.8 steals in leading Southwest to a 22-4 record and a berth in the Class A state semifinals. As a junior, Williams played in Southwest's final five games after returning from a knee injury suffered during summer basketball in June of 2022. She averaged 10.6, 1.0 rebound and 1.6 steals over those five games to help the 14-11 Silver Hawks to a state tournament berth in 2023.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a sophomore, Williams averaged 11.9 points, 3.2 assists and 3.0 steals to earn second-team Super-State and All-Nebraska honors. She was also the 2022 Lincoln Journal Star Girls Basketball Player of the Year. She helped the Silver Hawks to a state runner-up finish by scoring 24 points in a quarterfinal win Omaha Central. Southwest finished with a 21-6 record that included a semifinal victory over Millard South, before suffering a loss to Fremont in the state championship game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Williams sparked an upstart Southwest team as a freshman, averaging 8.9 points, 1.9 assists and 2.6 steals in helping the Silver Hawks to a 19-3 record and a berth in the Class A state tournament first round. Williams earned honorable-mention Class A all-state accolades from both the Lincoln Journal Star and Omaha World-Herald in 2021.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She led Southwest to a Class A state semifinal appearance as a senior softball player in the fall of 2023, leading Class A with 18 runs scored while batting .450 with 18 RBIs and 17 stolen bases. She earned first-team All-Nebraska and Super-State recognition along with first-team Class A all-state honors as a senior. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She missed her junior softball season in the fall of 2022 after suffering a knee injury in summer basketball. As a sophomore, Williams batted .362 with six home runs, seven doubles and 29 RBIs as a shortstop and center fielder to help the Silver Hawks to a Class A state championship in the fall of 2021. She was an honorable-mention Class A all-state choice as a sophomore. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She was a member of Lincoln Southwest's soccer program that advanced to the Class A state soccer tournament in the spring of 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Lloyd and Amy Williams, Kennadi has a younger sister, Bentli. (2022)\u003C/li>\n\u003C/ul>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Junior (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Australian National Program member Jessica Petrie (pronounced PEA-tree) returns for her third season inside for the Huskers. The 6-2 forward from Gold Coast, Australia, filled the void inside at power forward left by the season-ending injury to the 2024 Big Ten Freshman of the Year Natalie Potts in November 2024. Petrie started 23 games for the Big Red as a sophomore alongside four-time All-Big Ten center Alexis Markowski. Petrie averaged 6.4 points and 4.4 rebounds to help Nebraska to its second straight NCAA Tournament.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 28 games in 2025-26, Petrie is averaging 11.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.0 steal. She missed Nebraska's win over Northwestern (Jan. 28) and did not make the trip to No. 11 Ohio State (Feb. 1) because of illness. She returned to action in a limited role at No. 8 Michigan (Feb. 4).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie, who has scored double figures 19 times this year, closed the regular season with 16 points and six rebounds in her fourth straight game coming off the bench in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28). She added her second double-double and third of her career with 10 points and 10 rebounds against Indiana in the Big Ten Tournament (March 4).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie's top scoring effort in Big Ten play came with 18 points and seven rebounds in a win over Indiana (Jan. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She erupted for a career-high 20 points to go with six rebounds, two assists, a block and a steal in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 17 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block at No. 14 Iowa (Jan. 1). She also had 17 points, four rebounds and two steals in an 87-56 run past Cal Baptist to close non-conference play (Dec. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie notched her first double-double of the year with 15 points and 10 rebounds in a 92-53 win over Bradley (Dec. 3). She added 15 points and six rebounds in a win over Illinois (Jan. 24).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 14 points with a career-high four three-pointers while adding a career-best three steals at Minnesota (Feb. 12). Petrie also had 14 points, seven rebounds and two blocks in an 87-35 run past Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie put up 12 points off the bench at Oregon (Feb. 19). She also had 12 points, three rebounds, four assists and two blocks in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched 11 points, four rebounds and two blocks in a 66-65 win at Washington (Feb. 22). She also had 11 points, four rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block in an 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12). Her effort against the Jays included a 70-foot buzzer-beating three at the end of the first quarter and making No. 3 on ESPN SportsCenter's Top Plays.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 11-point efforts in a season-opening win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3) and in a win over Virginia in the Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie produced 10 points against No. 4 UCLA (Jan. 11), at Penn State (Dec. 6) and against ORU (Nov. 19).\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Petrie averaged 6.4 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists over 33 games with 23 starts.She replaced fellow sophomore forward Natalie Potts - the 2024 Big Ten Freshman of the Year - in the starting lineup after Potts was lost for the season to a knee injury against North Alabama (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie produced three solid efforts in the Big Ten Tournament, including 11 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks in a win over Illinois (March 6). Petrie scored nine points in the fourth quarter including the go-ahead three-pointer with 1:36 left to help the Huskers rally from a nine-point third-quarter deficit.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 8.7 points and 3.7 rebounds in the tournament while hitting 12-of-19 shots (.632) from the field.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie closed the season with six points and three assists against Louisville in the NCAA Tournament first round (March 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She surged in the heart of conference play, producing her third straight double-figure scoring effort with a career-high 15 points to go with seven rebounds and three assists in a win over Wisconsin (Jan. 20). Petrie hit 6-of-8 shots, including a career-best 3-of-4 three-pointers against the Badgers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>It followed a 13-point, six-board effort in a road win at Iowa (Jan. 16). She started the stretch with 12 points and a career-high nine rebounds in a win at Rutgers (Jan. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with back-to-back double-digit scoring efforts, including 11 points, eight rebounds and a career-high seven assists in a win at Northwestern (March 2). It followed her first career double-double with 10 points and a career-high 10 rebounds against Washington (Feb. 23). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie had an 11-point, six-rebound effort in NU's upset at No. 17 Maryland (Feb. 13). She added a career-high five blocks - all in the second half - to go with three points and six rebounds in NU's win over Oregon (Feb. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She ranked second among the Huskers in conference-only rebounding (5.4 rpg) while adding 7.4 points per game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie put up 14 points and two blocks to go with five rebounds in just 16 minutes in a win over North Alabama (Nov. 19) in the moments after the season-ending knee injury to Potts. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie followed with her first career start in place of the injured Potts at Creighton (Nov. 22). Petrie finished with nine points, two rebounds and two assists against the Jays.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added her second start against Kansas City (Nov. 26), before making her third start at No. 1 UCLA. She finished with seven points against the Bruins, while wearing jersey No. 45 instead her red No. 12, which was damaged. Petrie, who wears her No. 12 in honor of her mother who was a professional player in Australia, was surprised by her parents who made the trip to Los Angeles to watch the Huskers over the holidays. A replacement No. 12 made it to Los Angeles for the next game at No. 4 USC (Jan. 1). She had eight points, three rebounds and a career-high two steals in a start against the Trojans. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie added six points and three rebounds while making a third consecutive start in a Big Ten win over Penn State (Jan. 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie put up six more points and three rebounds in NU's win over No. 20 Michigan State (Jan. 8). She scored all six points in a 15-0 second-quarter Big Red run.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2023-24)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Petrie produced back-to-back season-high 11-point efforts in wins over UNCW and Michigan State. She scored 11 points on 5-of-7 shooting in 12 first-half minutes in a win at MSU (Dec. 9). Petrie’s production came in place of All-Big Ten post Alexis Markowski, who missed much of the first half with foul trouble.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie established her career high with 11 points on 5-of-9 shooting, while adding four rebounds, an assist and a steal in a win over UNCW (Dec. 5). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had nine points and her first career steal in a win over Florida Atlantic (Nov. 29). She added eight points and a season-best six rebounds in a win over Alcorn State (Nov. 14), after tipping the season with seven points and three boards in a win over Northwestern State.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 3.8 points and 2.0 rebounds in nearly 11 minutes per game on the season. She had a strong seven-point effort in a road win at Michigan (Feb. 6). It came after a nine-point performance against Rutgers (Feb. 3).\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>Petrie closed the regular season with a solid seven-point performance at Illinois (March 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She competed for Australia in three different age divisions (U16, U17, U18) in the summer of 2022 and at the U19 World Cup in Madrid, Spain (July 15-23, 2023).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie, from Gold Coast, Queensland, averaged 17.6 points, 9.1 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.1 steals through seven games for the Basketball Centre of Excellence in Australia’s semi-professional NBL1 East Division in 2023.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Petrie starred at three levels for the Australian National Team in the summer of 2022. She averaged 7.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists over five games for the Australian U18 National Team at the FIBA Asian Championship in Bengaluru, India in September. She helped the Australia Gems to a gold medal with a championship game win over China. In a semifinal victory over Taipei, Petrie produced 11 points and three rebounds, after getting eight points, eight rebounds and three assists in a win over Korea.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Her performance at the U18 level followed a seven-game stint with the Australian U17 National Team at the World Cup in Debrecen, Hungary, July 9-17, 2022. She averaged 12.3 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists, posting double-doubles against both Belgium and Spain before capping the World Cup with 15 points and nine rebounds in a win over Hungary.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>At the 2022 FIBA U16 Asian Championship in Amman, Jordan, June 24-30, Petrie averaged eight points, five rebounds and four assists. In the championship game against Japan, Petrie finished with 12 points, six rebounds and a game-high six assists to help the Sapphires to a 59-58 victory. Her performance against Japan followed a near triple-double in a semifinal win over Korea, when she produced 13 points, nine rebounds and 10 assists.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Petrie also starred at Lake Ginninderra College, leading the Lakers to the Australian Schools Championship at Gold Coast in December of 2022. Petrie was named to the tournament's all-star five and was the Defensive MVP of the tournament. She averaged 23.8 points, 16.8 rebounds and 6.4 assists at the tournament.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The daughter of Anthony and Sarah (Berry) Petrie, Jessica has younger sisters, Emma and Holly, and a younger brother, William. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Jessica's father was a long-time forward (2007-18) in Australia's NBL, helping the Adelaide 36ers to NBL Grand Final appearances in both 2014 and 2016. In 2009-10, he was second-team All-NBL and was named the NBL's Most Improved Player. He is currently coaching for the Gold Coast Rollers in NBL1. Her mother, Sarah, was a two-time WNBL champion with the Canberra Capitals.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Jess is majoring in communication studies and earned Academic All-District VII honors from the College Sports Communicators in 2025. She also earned Academic All-Big Ten recognition and claimed an Arthur Ashe Jr. Sports Scholar Award in 2025. (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Callin Hake (pronounced CAL-in HAKE)  has been counted on to provide leadership and stability in Nebraska's backcourt in her fourth season as a Husker in 2025-26. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The 5-8 senior from Victoria, Minn., has averaged 7.1 points, 2.5 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 steals through 30 games. She also leads NU with a school-record 31 charges drawn.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She tied career highs with 17 points and five three-pointers - all in the first half - in NU's 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake produced a 13-point effort on 3-of-6 three-point shooting in a win over Northwestern (Jan. 28). It was her eighth double-digit scoring performance of the season. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened the regular season with 13 points on 4-of-4 shooting from the field in a 103-46 win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3). Hake added 13 on 4-of-6 shooting, including 3-of-4 from long range, in NU's 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12). She added a game-high four assists to go along with three rebounds against the Jays.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored 11 points on 3-of-5 three-point shooting in a win over Purdue (Jan. 4). She also drew two charges. She added 11 points, six assists, two rebounds and two steals in Nebraska's Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship game win over Virginia (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake had 10 points while drawing two more charges against No. 4 UCLA (Jan. 11). She also put up 10 points to go with six rebounds, five assists, a steal and three charges drawn in an 87-56 win over Cal Baptist (Dec. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with eight points in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28). She also had eight points against No. 17 USC (Dec. 29) and eight more in a win over ORU (Nov. 19). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake had a career-high eight assists while snagging two steals in a Big Ten-opening win over Penn State (Dec. 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added seven points, seven rebounds and six assists with no turnovers in a 92-53 run past Bradley (Dec. 3). She also had seven points, four rebounds, five assists and her third career block in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had six points and five assists in an 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14). Hake had five points, seven assists and four steals in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Last season, Hake played in all 33 games with 30 starts for the Huskers while helping Nebraska to a second straight NCAA Tournament bid.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake also played a leading role in Nebraska's 2024 NCAA Tournament bid that included a trip to the second round after appearing in the 2024 Big Ten Championship Game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>An outstanding all-around player who provides both a high basketball IQ and high energy to the Big Red backcourt, Hake owns 146 career threes while shooting nearly 36 percent from long range in her career.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake is also one of the Big Ten Conference's top student-athlete leaders. The chair of the Big Ten Student-Athlete Issues Commission in 2025-26, she also represented Nebraska on the Big Ten SAIC in 2024-25 while serving as the President of the Nebraska Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. Her leadership off the court and her outstanding academic performance earned her recognition as Nebraska's Big Ten Outstanding Sportsmanship Award winner across all of its female sports in 2024-25.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"Callin is a versatile guard who can bring a lot of things to our team on the basketball court,\" Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said. \"I love that she is committed to playing hard at both ends of the court. Not only is Callin the perfect fit for us on the court, but she fits our family. She is not afraid to work and understands how to be a great teammate.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Junior (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Hake was counted on for leadership and stability in Nebraska's backcourt in her third season as a Husker in 2024-25. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake started 30 of NU's 33 games, helping lead the Big Red to a second consecutive NCAA Tournament appearance. She averaged 6.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.3 steals. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake sank a pair of free throws with 11 seconds left to seal Nebraska's come-from-behind win over Illinois (March 6). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She tied career highs with 17 points and seven assists in a win over Oregon (Feb. 19). She hit back-to-back threes in overtime to help the Huskers overcome a 14-point third-quarter deficit.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She established a career high with 17 points in a win over North Alabama (Nov. 19), when she hit 5-of-7 shots from the field and all six of her free throws. She added five rebounds, two assists and two steals.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake contributed a strong effort with 16 points, a season-high six rebounds, four assists and two steals in a win over Penn State (Jan. 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also had 16 points on a career-high five threes in a win over Kansas City (Nov. 26), before adding 12 points, six rebounds, three assists and a career-high four steals in a win over Lindenwood (Dec. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake put up double figures for the third straight game with 11 points and a trio of three-pointers in Nebraska’s Big Ten-opening win over Minnesota (Dec. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched eight double-digit scoring games on the season, including 10 points and four assists in Nebraska's 91-71 upset at No. 17 Maryland (Feb. 13). Hake added 12 points to go with four rebounds and three steals against No. 12 Ohio State (Jan. 26). She had 10 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals in a win over Chattanooga (Dec. 15).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake averaged career bests of 6.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.3 steals, including nine points on 3-of-4 three-point shooting, five assists and three steals in Nebraska's win over Wisconsin (Jan. 20).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake opened 2024-25 with a start in Nebraska’s 88-48 win over Omaha (Nov. 4). She scored four points while matching career highs with four assists and three steals in the win over the Mavericks.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She played an outstanding floor game while assuming point guard duties in a win over Southeastern Louisiana (Nov. 9). Hake finished with six points, six rebounds and a career-high seven assists in the win over the Lady Lions.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had three points, three rebounds and four assists in a win over Southern (Nov. 12). Hake came off the bench in the win over South Dakota, dishing out four assists while grabbing three rebounds and a steal. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2023-24)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Hake made greater contributions to Nebraska's lineup in her second season as a Husker. One of the Big Ten's most improved players, Hake averaged 6.1 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.9 assists, producing more points (+79), rebounds (+60), assists (+49), steals (+15) and blocks (+1) than 2022-23. She also hit 37.7 percent (40-106) of her three-point attempts.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched her seventh double-figure scoring performance with 15 points, including 12 in the second half, in Nebraska's 64-56 win over Purdue at the Big Ten Tournament (March 7). Hake averaged 8.3 points and 3.3 rebounds, while hitting 7-of-15 threes (.467) in Nebraska's run to a Big Ten Tournament runner-up finish.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake had 11 points and four rebounds at No. 5 Iowa (Jan. 27). She had a career-high-tying 16 points on 4-of-7 three-point shooting in NU's first-ever home win over Maryland (Dec. 31).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake scored 14 points and notched seven rebounds and three steals in a win over Alcorn State (Nov. 14). She opened the season with 12 points on perfect 4-for-4 three-point shooting in a win over Northwestern State (Nov. 6). She contributed 11 points and a career-high four assists in a win over Florida Atlantic (Nov. 29), before pitching in 10 points, five boards, a career-high-tying four assists and her first career block in a win over UNCW (Dec. 5). Hake added nine big points on 3-of-5 three-point shooting in a Big Ten-opening win at Michigan State (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2022-23)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Hake was a regular contributor for the Nebraska women's basketball team as a true freshman in 2022-23.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She appeared in 31 of Nebraska's 33 games, while making her first career start in a victory at Purdue (Jan. 18). She scored eight points in place of Maddie Krull in Nebraska's 71-64 win over the Boilermakers. Hake, who averaged 4.3 points and 1.3 rebounds, produced four double-figure scoring efforts in a five-game span early in Big Ten play.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake put up a season-high 16 points on 4-of-6 three-point shooting in Nebraska's run past Penn State (Jan. 11). She opened the stretch with 11 points on 3-of-4 three-point shooting against No. 14 Michigan (Dec. 28), before capping the group of double-digit efforts with 11 more points on 3-of-6 three-point shooting against No. 3 Ohio State. She added 10 points on a pair of threes in an overtime setback at No. 4 Indiana (Jan. 1). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In Nebraska's second-round WNIT win over Northern Iowa (March 19), Hake stepped up with six points, three rebounds and two assists off the bench after starter Sam Haiby suffered a lower leg injury that knocked her out for the rest of the game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake scored six points on a pair of threes in wins over Houston Christian (Nov. 11) and Texas A&M-Corpus Christi (Nov. 25). She opened her career with three points, three rebounds, an assist and a steal in a win over Omaha (Nov. 7). She also knocked down a three-pointer at No. 20 Creighton (Nov. 15). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Overall, Hake connected on at least one three-pointer in 20 games, including nine games with multiple threes.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>A four-time first-team All-Metro West Conference selection for the Storm, Hake was also a four-time Chanhassen team most valuable player. She captured Metro West Player-of-the-Year honors as a senior in 2021-22 after averaging 22.2 points per game. She became Chanhassen's first career 2,000-point scorer after a 26-point, 12-rebound performance against Cooper on Jan. 31, 2022. That performance followed a then-career-high and Chanhassen-record 37 points in a win over Waconia (Jan. 30). She topped that mark with 38 points in a win over New Prague (Feb. 18).  \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A McDonald's All-America Midwest nominee, Hake earned honorable-mention All-Metro accolades from the Minneapolis Star-Tribune as a senior. She was also named to the Metro West Conference All-Defensive Team before capping her high school career by playing in the Minnesota Girls Basketball Coaches Association All-Star Series. She claimed the MGBCA Three-Point Championship by draining 14 three-pointers in 45 seconds.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior in a COVID-shortened 2020-21 season, Hake averaged 21.5 points per game. She averaged 22.2 points per game as a sophomore and 20.4 points per contest as a freshman at Class 4A Chanhassen.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She entered her junior season with high school career totals of 1,633 points, 442 rebounds, 147 steals and 120 assists. She added 599 points as a senior to finish with 2,232 career points.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake spent six years competing for the UAA Minnesota Fury, helping the team to a national runner-up finish. She was a first-team Minnesota AAU all-state selection in 2021. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also earned three letters in track and field at Chanhassen. She was also involved as the DECA President and won the DECA Outstanding Student Award in 2021-22. She was also a two-year National Honor Society member and a four-year Key Club member.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Chad and Jill Hake, Callin was born in Waconia, Minn. She has an older brother, Carson, who was a senior infielder for the North Dakota State baseball team in 2024. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A double-major in management and marketing at Nebraska, Callin was a College Sports Communicators Academic All-District VII selection in both 2024 and 2025. A 2025 Big Ten Distinguished Scholar, she  claimed Academic All-Big Ten honors in both 2024 and 2025. She was also a member of the Chi Alpha Sigma Honor Society in 2025. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hake has earned seven spots on the Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll and is a three-time member of the Tom Osborne Citizenship Team. She also captured a prestigious Sam Foltz 27 Hero Leadership Award in 2024. (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Natalie Potts hoped to return to the Nebraska lineup in her third year as a Husker, but announced on Jan. 29 that she will not return to the court competitively in 2025-26. She will redshirt and plans to return in 2026-27 with a possibility of three years of eligibility.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The 6-2 redshirt sophomore from O'Fallon, Mo., suffered a season-ending knee injury in Nebraska's fifth game of 2024-25.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through the first four games last season, the 2024 Big Ten Freshman of the Year  was performing at an all-conference level, averaging team bests of 17.5 points and 8.0 rebounds while shooting nearly 70 percent from the field, including 72.7 percent from three-point range.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She sustained the injury midway through the second quarter of Nebraska’s win over North Alabama (Nov. 19) and was lost for the season. She underwent surgery Dec. 4.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts was replaced in the Husker lineup by classmate Jessica Petrie, and Potts continued to play an integral role in Nebraska's season. Not only did she help keep the Huskers focused on their run to the NCAA Tournament from the sideline, she focused herself on a diligent rehab after surgery.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>“Natalie is a great fit for us both on and off the basketball court,\" Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said. \"She has an incredible motor, and her competitive spirit matches the values we have for our team. She is versatile and a proven winner from one of the most successful high school programs in the country.”\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Potts was the only Husker to score in double figures in each of NU’s first four games of 2024-25, before being sidelined by a season-ending knee injury against North Alabama in Nebraska's fifth game (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She tied her career high with 22 points on 8-of-10 shooting to go with seven rebounds in just 23 minutes in a record-setting win over South Dakota (Nov. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>It followed her sixth career double-double with 17 points and a game-high 12 rebounds in a win over Southern (Nov. 12). Potts also put up 17 points to go with seven rebounds on a career-best 4-of-5 three-point shooting in a win over Southeastern Louisiana (Nov. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts opened 2024-25 with 14 points in an 88-48 run past Omaha (Nov. 4). She added six rebounds, an assist, a block and a steal.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She underwent knee surgery Dec. 4, 2024.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2023-24)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The 2024 Big Ten Freshman of the Year as voted by the conference coaches, Potts was a unanimous choice on the Big Ten All-Freshman Team and claimed honorable-mention All-Big Ten accolades from the league media.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The eight-time Big Ten Freshman of the Week ranked among the top freshman scorers (10.2 ppg) and rebounders (5.5 rpg) in the conference. She started all 35 games for the Huskers, which set the school record for most consecutive starts by a freshman in school history. Potts was one of only 10 freshmen in Husker history to start every game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts produced five double-doubles in her rookie campaign, including 15 points, 11 rebounds and three blocks in a Big Ten quarterfinal win over Michigan State (March 8). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts, who tied the Nebraska Big Ten Tournament record with nine blocks over four games, followed with her second career 20-point performance, just missing a double-double with 21 points and nine rebounds in the Big Ten Championship Game against No. 3 Iowa (March 10). It was her 20th game scoring in double figures in 2023-24.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced game highs of 18 points, including 13 in the third quarter, and 10 rebounds in Nebraska’s win over Northwestern (Feb. 20). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She led the Huskers with game highs of 13 points and 10 boards in a win over Michigan (Jan. 17). Potts produced 17 points and a career-high 13 rebounds in NU’s first-ever win over Maryland (Dec. 31). She had 13 points and 12 boards in the second half alone against the Terps. She also went 7-for-7 at the line, including 4-for-4 in the final 45 seconds to seal the win.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She followed with 16 points - all in the second half - in NU’s win at Wisconsin (Jan. 4). She had an 11-point, six-rebound effort that included a career-high four steals in a win over Purdue (Jan. 31), before adding 12 big points in a win at Michigan (Feb. 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts produced a 14-point, six-rebound effort in Nebraska’s upset of No. 2 Iowa (Feb. 11) when she had eight points and five rebounds to spark a comeback from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit. She earned her sixth Big Ten freshman honor on Feb. 12.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She claimed her seventh freshman award by averaging 15.0 points, 8.5 rebounds and 2.0 steals in wins over Northwestern (Feb. 20) and Minnesota (Feb. 24) to close out Nebraska’s home schedule with a pair of wins.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts, who produced six double-digit rebound efforts, led Nebraska and all Big Ten freshmen with her .489 field goal percentage. She also ranked among Big Ten freshman leaders with her 82.9 free throw percentage (63-76).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced 11 double-digit scoring games in Big Ten play and two more in the Big Ten Tournament.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched her first career double-double with 12 points and 12 boards in a win over FAU (Nov. 29), before adding 13 points in a win over Georgia Tech (Dec. 2). She closed NU’s three-game stand with 11 points and eight rebounds in a win over UNCW (Dec. 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts opened her college career with 10 points, five rebounds, an assist, a block and two steals in a win over Northwestern State (Nov. 6). She was even better in her first road game, going for 15 points on 6-of-7 shooting, including a three-pointer, while adding two more steals and a block in a win at Wyoming (Nov. 10) to capture the inaugural Big Ten Freshman-of-the-Week award of 2023-24 (Nov. 13).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>After getting seven points, 11 rebounds and a career-high three blocks against Alcorn State (Nov. 14), she pumped in 16 points against No. 22 Creighton (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts led NU to a win over Lamar with a career-high 22 points on 9-of-10 shooting at the St. Pete Showcase. Potts earned her second Big Ten Freshman of the Week (Nov. 27). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts pitched in 10 points, five boards and two blocks in a win at Michigan State (Dec. 9) on her way to her third Big Ten Freshman of the Week honor (Dec. 11). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She claimed her fourth Big Ten honor (Jan. 8) after averaging 12.5 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 steals against Wisconsin and No. 14 Indiana. Potts added a fifth weekly honor (Jan. 15) by averaging 9.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.0 steals against Illinois and Minnesota.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Potts averaged 18.7 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game as a senior for Incarnate Word Academy in Bel Nor, Mo., which won its sixth consecutive Missouri state championship in 2023. She capped her career with a 32-0 record, a third straight Class 6 state title and a No. 6 final national ranking from MaxPreps.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The two-time Missouri High School Player of the Year, Potts showed explosive all-around ability, while providing a winning attitude.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts led Incarnate Word Academy to three consecutive Missouri state championships (no 2020 state tournament because of COVID-19) and a nation’s best 100-game winning streak to close her prep career. She led the Red Knights to a 117-4 record during her four high school seasons, including a 32-0 mark in Class 6, as Incarnate Word finished No. 6 nationally by MaxPreps and No. 10 in the final ESPN SCNext national rankings in 2022-23.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts captured Missouri MaxPreps Player of the Year honors in both 2021 and 2023, while adding a Gatorade Player of the Year award as a sophomore in 2021. She was also the St. Louis Post-Dispatch Metro Player of the Year in both 2021 and 2023.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts closed her high school career with 2,108 points and 1,008 rebounds in four seasons - just the third player in Missouri high school history to reach the combined milestones of 2,000 points and 1,000 boards. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced 19.3 points, 8.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.5 blocks per game while hitting 61.9 percent of her shots from the floor as a junior to lead Missouri Hall of Fame Head Coach Dan Rolfes' team to a 32-0 record, another Class 6 state championship and recognition as the Blue Star Media 25 national champion in 2021-22. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts averaged 20.7 points and 9.3 rebounds as a sophomore to earn Gatorade and MaxPreps Missouri Player-of-the-Year honors after leading Incarnate Word Academy to a Class 6 state championship in 2021. She was also the St. Louis Metro Area Player of the Year. Incarnate Word Academy finished No. 20 in the final espnW national rankings with a perfect 29-0 record.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also broke the Incarnate Word Academy single-game scoring record with 40 points on 19-of-21 shooting in a win over Ladue on Feb. 3, 2021. The previous record was held by two-time UConn first-team All-American Napheesa Collier. Potts finished her career with four 30-point games and 36 career double-doubles.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts opened her high school career with averages of 10.1 points and 8.3 rebounds as a freshman in 2019-20.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Potts, who played AAU basketball for Phee Elite, was ranked as the No. 1 recruit in the state of Missouri by Prep Girls Hoops.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The daughter of Eric and Sharon Potts, Natalie was born in St. Louis, Mo. She has an older brother, Kyle, and a sister, Sarah. Natalie is a management major and earned Academic All-Big Ten recognition in 2025. She is also a four-time Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll selection.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A two-time member of the Tom Osborne Citizenship Team, Potts is also a representative on the Nebraska Student-Athlete Advisory Committee in 2025-26.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She selected Nebraska over Gonzaga.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"I chose Nebraska because I loved the community and the family feel. Prince earned first-team All-Big Ten honors from league media and second-team accolades from the Big Ten coaches after an outstanding sophomore season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 30 games, the Nancy Lieberman Award candidate is averaging 17.4 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.5 assists while hitting 53.4 percent of her shots, including 45.2 percent of her threes.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince closed the regular season with her first career double-double with 14 points and a career-high 11 rebounds, while matching her career highs with eight assists and two blocks in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She captured MVP honors in leading Nebraska to the Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket title with a career-high-tying 30 points on 12-of-17 shooting in a championship game win over Virginia. In a head-to-head matchup with Cavalier All-American Kymora Johnson, Prince outscored the first-team All-ACC guard 18-2 in the first half. Prince averaged 24.0 points and 6.5 assists in two games, while hitting 20-of-31 shots.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened the tournament with 18 points and a season-high seven assists in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince erupted for a career-high 30 points on 13-of-18 shooting, including 4-of-6 threes, in NU's 103-58 win over Oral Roberts (Nov. 19). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince, who owns 10 20-point efforts on the season and 16 in her career, produced 22 points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals, while draining the game-winning three-pointer with seven seconds left in Nebraska's 66-65 win at Washington (Feb. 22).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She has 26 double-figure scoring efforts this season and 50 in her career. She is one of the nation's best free throw shooters (.904), including a school-record streak of 56 straight makes that ended with her first attempt against Iowa (Feb. 16). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced a 28-point performance in a win over Northwestern when she hit 10-of-15 shots, including 2-of-3 threes and all six of her free throws while adding six rebounds and six assists against just one turnover. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince put up 27 points on 10-of-18 shooting at No. 14 Iowa (Jan. 1). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She pumped in a game-high 23 points on 10-of-13 shooting in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8), after opening the regular season with 19 points and five rebounds in a 103-46 pounding of Northwestern State (Nov. 3). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 20 points and six assists with no turnovers in Nebraska's 101-83 run past Penn State (Dec. 6) to open Big Ten play. Prince led Nebraska with 20 and seven assists, including 11 points and four assists in the fourth quarter, in NU's 78-73 win over Indiana (Jan. 8). She added 20 points and eight assists against Indiana in the Big Ten Tournament (March 4).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince produced 20 points on 6-of-9 shooting in a win over Illinois (Jan. 24). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince had 18 points, seven rebounds and three assists in an 84-50 victory over Creighton (Nov. 12). She led Nebraska with 18 points and seven assists in a loss to No. 17 USC (Dec. 29). She also had 18 points and five assists at Oregon (Feb. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 17 points on 4-of-6 three-point shooting while adding five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block in a Big Ten win over Purdue (Jan. 4). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince also had 17 points on 7-of-9 shooting to go with five assists and four rebounds in a 92-53 win over Bradley (Dec. 3). She pitched in 16 points in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16), and got 16 more to go with four rebounds and four assists at No. 15 Michigan State (Jan. 15).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 13 points, six rebounds and six assists in an 85-44 run past Illinois State (Dec. 14). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince managed 12 points, five rebounds and six assists at No. 11 Ohio State (Feb. 1).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 11 points in a win over Cal Baptist (Dec. 21). She added 11 points and tied her season high with five steals at Wisconsin (Jan. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>“Britt is an extremely gifted athlete and when you partner that with an intense passion for basketball, a work ethic that is unmatched, high character, and a winning mindset, the result is something special,\" Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said. \"It has been amazing to watch Britt utilize her unique talents to accomplish so much already in her basketball journey, and we cannot wait for that to continue into her college career here as a Husker. Britt’s decision to stay home and represent her home state says a lot about Husker Nation and how special it is to play for Nebraska.”\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2024-25)\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Prince earned a spot on the Big Ten All-Freshman Team and honorable-mention All-Big Ten accolades from both the coaches and the media after averaging 13.4 points, 4.0 rebounds and team bests of 3.8 assists and 1.7 steals. She was even better over three games at the Big Ten Tournament, averaging team highs of 17.0 points and 5.3 assists on 55.9 percent shooting, including 75 percent (9-12) from long range.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince capped the conference tournament by tying a career high with 24 points, including four three-pointers, to go along with six assists in a quarterfinal loss to No. 4 UCLA (March 7). She opened the Big Ten Tournament with 10 points and five assists in a win over Rutgers (March 5), before leading NU with 17 points and five assists in a win over Illinois (March 6). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She capped her freshman season by leading Nebraska with 14 points and six assists against Louisville in the NCAA Tournament first round (March 21). It was her 23rd double-figure scoring effort of the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She shared Nebraska's team MVP honors with senior Alexis Markowski, before being named Nebraska's Female Freshman Athlete of the Year across all sports for 2024-25.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince missed Nebraska's win over Oregon (Feb. 19) and a loss to Washington (Feb. 23) with a lower leg injury suffered in the closing minutes at Illinois (Feb. 16). She returned for 15 points and six assists in a win at Northwestern in the regular-season finale (March 2). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>An outstanding defender, Prince was the first Husker freshman since Nicole Kubik (1996-97) to record 50 steals while ranking among Big Ten leaders with 1.7 steals per game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched six 20-point efforts, including a career-high 24 points to lead Nebraska to a Big Ten road win at Rutgers (Jan. 12). She also had six boards and three assists at Rutgers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince added a 23-point performance in a road win at Purdue (Jan. 30) when she closed out the win with NU's final nine points.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had a game-high 22 points on a career-high five threes, while adding seven rebounds, five assists and a career-high six steals in a career-high 41 minutes in Nebraska's 87-84 OT win at Iowa (Jan. 16). Her performance against the Hawkeyes earned her Big Ten Freshman-of-the-Week honors (Jan. 20) and USBWA National Freshman of the Week (Jan. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 23 points on 10-of-13 shooting to go with four assists, two steals and a block in Nebraska’s record-setting 113-70 run past South Dakota (Nov. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince had 20 points and six rebounds at Creighton (Nov. 22). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had a solid 13-point, four-rebound effort that included a career-high eight assists in an upset win at No. 17 Maryland (Feb. 13). Prince added eight more assists to go with nine points at Illinois (Feb. 16), before suffering a lower leg injury in the closing minutes.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince put up a 14-point, seven-rebound effort that included three steals in a win over Wisconsin (Jan. 20), before getting eight points, eight rebounds, three assists and three steals against No. 12 Ohio State (Jan. 26). She scored 11 points at Indiana (Feb. 2) and 10 points against Michigan (Feb. 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 10 points in NU's win over No. 20 Michigan State (Jan. 8). It followed a 13-point performance that included four steals in a win over Penn State (Jan. 5). She also had 10 points and a career-high-tying eight rebounds to go with four assists at No. 4 USC (Jan. 1). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She led all scorers with 19 points, including a trio of three-pointers, to go with five rebounds in a win over Tarleton State (Dec. 11). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 14 points in a win over Lindenwood (Dec. 3), after getting 13 in a win over Kansas City (Nov. 26). She also had 13 points, six assists and two blocks in a win over North Alabama (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince opened her career with 10 points, a game-high five assists and two steals as a starter in a win over Omaha (Nov. 4), before missing NU’s win over Southeastern Louisiana (Nov. 9) with a lower leg injury. She returned with six points, three rebounds, four assists and three steals in a win over Southern (Nov. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Prince produced one of the best senior seasons in Nebraska high school history, averaging 27.0 points, 10.3 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.9 steals to capture her second straight Nebraska High School Player-of-the-Year honors from both Gatorade and MaxPreps in 2024. She led the state in both scoring and assists as a senior. Prince closed her career with a Nebraska Class B scoring record of 2,491 career points, surpassing previous record-holder Jordan Hooper, who was a first-team All-American at Nebraska in 2014, after a standout prep career at Alliance High School. Prince's 2,491 points rank No. 2 all-time across all classes in state high school history. Prince also totaled 271 career points at the state tournament, matching Hooper for second on the state tournament scoring list.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>An honorable-mention All-American by both the Naismith Trophy and MaxPreps as a senior, Prince was the No. 16 recruit by Prospects Nation and No. 28 by ESPN before signing with the Huskers on Nov. 8, 2023.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince averaged 24.2 points, 8.6 rebounds and 6.2 assists while hitting 59 percent of her shots from the floor, including 46 percent of her three-pointers, and 92 percent of her free throws as a junior at Elkhorn North in 2022-23 to earn her first state player of the year awards.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince was a four-time first-team Super State and All-Nebraska selection while leading the Wolves to four consecutive Class B state championships while playing for her mother and head coach, Ann Prince. At the 2023 state tournament, Prince totaled 84 points on 29-of-40 shooting, including 10-of-14 from long range. She was also a perfect 16-for-16 at the free throw line. During the regular season, Prince recorded a triple-double with 33 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a win over Hastings.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Prince capped her career with 17 points and 12 rebounds in a low-scoring 49-47 championship game victory over Omaha Skutt, which came after producing a triple-double with 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in a semifinal victory over Beatrice. Prince scored a career-high 42 points in the 2023-24 season opener, before tying her school record with 42 points in a 71-53 win over No. 2 Skutt (Jan. 6) to become the Class B all-time scoring leader, surpassing Husker first-team All-American Jordan Hooper's previous mark (2,078). The next day, Nebraska retired Hooper's No. 35 jersey.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 23.4 points per game as a freshman and 24.1 points per game as a sophomore.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She capped her high school career with a Nebraska Coaches Association All-Star Game record 32 points to go with 13 rebounds and six assists at Lincoln North Star on July 24, 2024. She hit 4-of-6 threes in the game to lead the Blue squad to a 99-87 win over the Red.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A talented all-around athlete, Prince finished fifth at the state cross country championships as a freshman, before winning state titles as a member of Elkhorn North's 4x400 relay team on the track as a freshman, sophomore and senior. She ran a personal-best time of 56.55 in the 400 in 2024. Prince won state gold in the 800-meter run as a sophomore, after taking silver in the event as a freshman. As a senior at the state championships in 2024, she ran a personal-best time of 2:16.62 in the 800 to finish fifth. She added relay golds in the 4x800 relay as a sophomore and senior after taking silver as a freshman.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>An Academic All-State selection in both cross country and basketball in 2023, Prince was a member of National Honor Society and the Honor Roll at Elkhorn North.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Mark and Ann Prince, Britt was born in Fremont, Neb.
