Amiah Hargrove has made a significant impact on Nebraska's fortunes in 2025-26. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a true freshman for the Huskers, Hargrove appeared in all 33 games with two starts and averaged 4.7 points and 3.7 rebounds per game to help Nebraska to the NCAA Tournament.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 29 games, Hargove is averaging 13.1 points and a team-best 5.4 rebounds in 24 minutes per game. She came off the bench in Nebraska's first 20 games this season before starting the past 10 contests. Her first starts came in place of Jessica Petrie, who was battling illness.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove has averaged 14.7 points and 5.2 rebounds in 27 minutes per game as a starter, including a double-double in a win over Northwestern (Jan. 28). She added the second-highest scoring total of her career with 24 points at No. 11 Ohio State (Feb. 1), before going for 23 points in a career-high 34 minutes against Indiana in the Big Ten Tournament (March 4). It was her fourth 20-point effort of the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with 18 points on 7-of-9 shooting in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove added 16 points and eight boards at No. 8 Michigan (Feb. 4) after notching her second double-double of the season with 13 points and a career-high-matching 11 rebounds in her first start of the year in a win over Northwestern (Jan. 28). She also had 13 points and six boards in a start at Minnesota (Feb. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove erupted for a career-high 26 points on 10-of-14 shooting while adding a career-best three steals in Nebraska's 101-83 run past Penn State (Dec. 6). She scored 19 points on 8-of-9 shooting, including 3-of-3 threes in the second half alone against the Lady Lions.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added a 21-point effort on 9-of-11 shooting at No. 15 Michigan State. She scored nine of NU's final 13 points to rally the Huskers from a 62-58 deficit to a 69-66 lead lead before NU fell on the road in the final seconds.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove had 15 points and a game-high eight rebounds in an 87-56 win over Cal Baptist (Dec. 21). She added 15 points and five rebounds on 7-of-10 shooting at Wisconsin (Jan. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove, who has scored in double figures 21 times this season, including nine times as a starter, put up 14 points in a 66-65 win at Washington (Feb. 22). She added 13 points on just five field goal attempts, including 3-of-3 three-point shooting in a win over Purdue (Jan. 4). She had missed the New Year's Day loss at No. 14 Iowa in the concussion protocol after being struck in the head twice in the fourth quarter in a loss to No. 17 USC (Dec. 29).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove had 12 points against No. 4 UCLA (Jan. 11). She had 11 points and five boards in an 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14). She also had 11 points, nine boards and a career-high three assists in a win over Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She earned a spot on the Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket All-Tournament Team after putting up 17 points, eight rebounds and two steals in 26 minutes off the bench to help the Huskers to a championship game win over Virginia (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>It followed an 11-point, six-rebound game in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24), as Hargrove averaged 14.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in two tournament games.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had 13 points and six rebounds in just 13 minutes in NU's 92-53 win over Bradley (Dec. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove produced her second career double-double with 12 points and 11 rebounds to go along with a career-high three steals in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8). Hargrove led Nebraska with a career-high 17 points on perfect shooting while adding a team-high seven rebounds off the bench in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In a key Big Ten win over Indiana (Jan. 8), Hargrove had nine points and six rebounds. She added six points and five boards in an 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12) and six points and six rebounds in a 103-58 win over ORU (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said Hargrove has a ton of upside in her basketball future.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"Amiah is a high achiever in everything she pursues, and we could not be more thrilled to be welcoming her to the Husker family,\" Williams said. \"Her size and athleticism combined with her versatile skill set make her the perfect fit for our team on the court. Her high character, work ethic and drive make her the perfect fit off the court. She has a bright, bright future, and we are so excited it will be while wearing Husker red.\"\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003Cdiv>\n\u003Cp> \u003C/p>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>As a true freshman for the Huskers, Hargrove appeared in all 33 games with two starts and averaged 4.7 points and 3.7 rebounds per game to help Nebraska to the NCAA Tournament.\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Hargrove produced the best game of her young career with her first double-double in a road win at Iowa (Jan. 16). She scored 10 points on 3-of-4 shooting, including a pair of threes, while adding career highs of 11 rebounds and two blocks against the Hawkeyes. She also played a career-high 28 minutes in the overtime victory to help the Huskers to their first win in Iowa City since 2018.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She nearly notched another double-double with 10 points and nine rebounds in just 17 minutes off the bench in Nebraska's NCAA Tournament first-round battle with Louisville in Fort Worth, Texas (March 21). Hargrove hit 3-of-5 shots, including a three-pointer, while going 3-for-4 at the free throw line against the Cardinals. She also pulled down four offensive boards, while adding an assist and a steal.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>For the season, she averaged 4.7 points and 3.7 rebounds per game while hitting 50 percent (17-34) of her three-pointers and 81.6 percent (31-38) of her free throws. She played in all 33 games with a pair of starts. In 18 conference games, Hargrove's numbers were nearly identical, averaging 4.6 points and 3.8 rebounds while shooting 51.8 percent from the field including 52.9 percent (9-17) from three-point range in 14 minutes per game.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened the Big Ten Tournament by tying her career high with 13 points while adding four rebounds in a first-round win over Rutgers (March 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove produced a career-high 13 points on 5-of-6 shooting in a win over Tarleton State (Dec. 11). It followed 10 points and a career-high eight rebounds in a Big Ten-opening win over Minnesota (Dec. 8). She added a team-high 12 points on 4-of-6 shooting at No. 1 UCLA (Dec. 29), before getting 11 points at Indiana (Feb. 2).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove scored in double figures seven times, including 10 points and seven boards in a win over Kansas City (Nov. 26). She made her first start in a win over Chattanooga (Dec. 15), when she pulled down seven rebounds.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added a strong seven-point, six-rebound performance in a win over No. 20 Michigan State (Jan. 8). Hargrove's effort included five big rebounds in the game's final five minutes to help Nebraska close out the victory.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove had eight points, three rebounds and two assists in a win over South Dakota (Nov. 16). She went 3-for-3 from the field, including a pair of three-pointers against the Coyotes.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Hargrove averaged 28.7 points, 10.7 rebounds, 2.9 steals and 1.9 assists as a senior at Illinois Class 1A Christopher High School. The No. 2 recruit in the state of Illinois, Hargrove was a three-time Southern Illinois Player of the Year and a four-time Class 1A all-state selection. She was also named to the MaxPreps Small Town All-America Team as a senior at Christopher (pop. 2,644), located approximately 100 miles southeast of St. Louis. She finished with 2,774 points and 1,096 career rebounds after averaging 25.8 points and 10.2 rebounds during her prep career. She also totaled more than 200 career steals while hitting more than 83 percent of her free throws.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior in 2022-23, Hargrove averaged 24.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.3 blocks while hitting 62.8 percent of her shots from the field to help Christopher High School to a Class 1A runner-up finish. The four-time Illinois Class 1A all-state selection was the 2023 Associated Press Illinois Class 1A Player of the Year and a three-time Southern Illinois Girls Basketball Player of the Year. She was also a three-time conference MVP and four-time all-conference selection.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A talented all-around athlete, Hargrove erupted for a career-high 55 points against Salem and 51 points against Cobden. She led Christopher High School to a state runner-up finish after capturing sectional and super-sectional titles in 2023. She also fueled the Bearcats to a trio of conference championships and two regional crowns.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove also has competed in volleyball, softball and track and field, while earning third-team Academic All-America honors. She was a member of the High Honor Roll and National Honor Society at Christopher.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She played AAU basketball for Bradley Beal Elite and was ranked as the No. 159 recruit in the nation by Blue Star Basketball.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Anthony and Ami Hargrove, Amiah was born in St. Louis, Mo. She has a younger sister, Aralynn, and an older brother, Tre Carroll, who is a senior basketball player at Xavier in 2025-26. He was a redshirt freshman on Florida Atlantic's 2023 NCAA Final Four team and played at FAU through 2024-25. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Amiah's father was an NFL defensive end from 2004 to 2013. He was drafted out of Georgia Tech by the St. Louis Rams and was a member of seven NFL teams, including the Super Bowl champion New Orleans Saints.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>A sociology major, Hargrove is a three-time Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll. She was also a member of the 2025 Tom Osborne Citizenship Team.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Hargrove selected Nebraska over Creighton, Missouri, Illinois and Marquette.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"I chose Nebraska because it was the perfect fit for me,\" Hargrove said. \"From the Lincoln community to the coaching staff, it instantly reminded me of home. (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Croatian Petra Bozan (pronounced PET-ruh, BO-jahn) is coming off a strong summer with the Croatian U20 National Team and hopes to work her way into a prominent role inside for the Huskers as a sophomore in 2025-26.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan, a 6-3 forward from Split, Croatia, was the primary backup to four-time All-Big Ten center Alexis Markowski in 2024-25, averaging 5.3 points and 2.8 rebounds while playing all 33 games for NCAA Tournament-bound NU.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan produced the best week of her career by averaging 14.5 points and 6.5 rebounds in Nebraska wins over Bradley and Penn State. She capped the week with a career-high 17 points on 8-of-12 shooting in NU's Big Ten-opening road win over the Lady Lions. She scored 11 straight points, including NU's first nine points of the fourth quarter to help the Huskers surge to a 101-83 win with a 36-point final period. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened the week with 12 points and nine boards in a 92-53 run past Bradley (Dec. 3).\n\u003Cdiv>Bozan notched her ninth double-figure scoring effort of the season with 12 points and six rebounds in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also had 11 points on 5-of-6 shooting in a start at Oregon (Feb. 19). She had 12 points on 4-of-6 shooting and a perfect 4-for-4 effort at the free throw line at No. 8 Michigan (Feb. 4). She added 11 points and four boards in a win over Illinois (Jan. 24).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had team highs of 14 points, six rebounds and three blocks in just 17 minutes in NU's 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan put up a then-career-high 13 points to go with six rebounds, two steals and a block in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8). She opened the regular season with 11 points and three rebounds in her first career start in a 103-46 win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan had eight points on 4-of-5 shooting to go with four rebounds in an 87-56 win over Cal Baptist to close non-conference play (Dec. 21). She also eight points and three rebounds in an 87-35 run past Omaha (Dec. 9). She had eight points, four rebounds and a career-high three assists at No. 15 Michigan State (Jan. 15).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 30 games, she is averaging 6.7 points and 3.4 rebounds. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 5.0 points and 2.0 rebounds in wins over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24) and Virginia (Nov. 25) in helping the Huskers to the Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket title.\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>She had four points and career highs of 10 rebounds and two assists in a 103-58 win over Oral Roberts (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan contributed nine points, three rebounds and two steals in Nebraska's 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In the summer, she earned a spot on the All-Star Five at the FIBA Eurobasket Division B Championships in Miskolc, Hungary (Aug. 2-10), averaging 13.3 points and 6.4 rebounds over seven games to help the Croatian U20 team to third place and a promotion to Division A.\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv> \u003C/div>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>\u003Cbr>Freshman (2024-25)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The final addition to the Nebraska roster for the 2024-25 season, Bozan arrived in Lincoln on Aug. 25, just in time for the start of fall classes the next day. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 7.3 points on 10-of-14 (.714) shooting in the Big Ten Tournament. She scored 11 points in a win over Illinois (March 6), after opening the tournament with nine points on 4-for-4 shooting including a three-pointer in a win over Rutgers (March 5).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She averaged 5.3 points and 2.8 rebounds in 11 minutes per game on the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan produced six double-figure scoring efforts on the year, including 12 points, four rebounds and a block in less than 13 minutes off the bench in a season-opening win over Omaha (Nov. 4) when she hit a pair of three-pointers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She tied her career high with 12 points to go with three rebounds and a block in 14 minutes at Indiana (Feb. 2).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan also had 10 points on 4-for-4 shooting in a win over Wisconsin (Jan. 20). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored 11 points on 4-for-4 shooting including a pair of three-pointers in a win over Southeastern Louisiana (Nov. 9), before adding 10 points on 5-of-7 shooting in a win over Lindenwood (Dec. 3). She followed with nine points on 3-of-5 shooting, including a three, while grabbing five rebounds in the Big Ten-opening win over Minnesota (Dec. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan ended the regular season with nine points and six boards in a win at Northwestern (March 2). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added eight big points and six rebounds in just 11 minutes in another Big Ten home win over Penn State (Jan. 5), before pitching in five points and two rebounds in NU's win over No. 20 Michigan State (Jan. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan contributed eight first-half points in place of Alexis Markowski, while adding four rebounds and a block to help Nebraska claim a Big Ten road win at Rutgers (Jan. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She pitched in eight points in a career-high 19 minutes in a win over Chattanooga (Dec. 15), before getting seven points at No. 1 UCLA (Dec. 29). Bozan had six points and a career-high seven boards in a win over Southern (Nov. 12), before notching four points, five rebounds and a career-high three blocks in a win over North Alabama (Nov. 19). She had four points and tied her career high with seven rebounds while adding her first two steals in a win over Kansas City (Nov. 26).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan brought extensive international experience with her to Nebraska, representing the Croatian U18 National Team at European championship events in the summers of 2023 and 2024. During the summer of 2023, Bozan earned an appearance on the All-Star Five at the U18 European Championships in Sofia, Bulgaria, after powering Croatia to the Division B title.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan averaged 16.1 points, 10.0 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 1.3 assists in leading Croatia at the FIBA U18 Women’s Eurobasket in Portugal (Aug. 3-11). She ranked third among all players in the 16-team tournament in rebounding, while ranking sixth in scoring.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Before Nebraska\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Bozan led Croatia in both points (113) and rebounds (70) over seven tournament games at the 2024 FIBA U18 Women's Eurobasket in Matsinhos, Portugal (Aug. 3-11). She ranked sixth among all players in the 16-team tournament in scoring (16.1 ppg) and third in rebounding (10.0 rpg). She added 1.6 blocks and 1.3 assists.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Against Turkey (Aug. 8), Bozan erupted for 25 points, 17 rebounds and two blocks in 36 minutes, going 10-of-16 from the field, including 3-of-6 from three-point range. She added a second double-double with 16 points and 12 rebounds in a win over Poland (Aug. 4), before putting up her first of two 20-point performances in the tournament with 21 points to go with nine rebounds against Belgium (Aug. 5). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>For the tournament, Bozan hit 48 percent of her field goal attempts, including 27.3 percent (6-22) of her threes, while knocking down 72.2 percent (13-18) of her free throws.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>During the 2023-24 season, Bozan competed for KAZL Split in Croatia's Premier League, averaging 15.6 points, 12.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.7 blocked shots over 22 games, to earn second-team All-Premier League honors. She hit 54.5 percent of her field goals and 73.6 percent of her free throws, helping KAZL Split to a 17-5 record. Her performances included a season-high 31 points on 14-of-21 shooting to go along with 10 rebounds and seven steals in a win over Zagreb (Oct. 28, 2023). It was one of her 17 double-doubles during the 22-game Premier League regular season. She pulled down a season-high 19 rebounds against Brod na Savi (Nov. 4, 2023).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Bozan averaged 12.4 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists for Croatia at the 2023 FIBA U18 European Championships. Her efforts in Sofia, Bulgaria included double-doubles against Greece and Macedonia before adding a third double-double with 20 points, 11 rebounds and four assists in the title game win over Luxembourg. She earned a spot on the tournament's All-Star Five to propel Croatia to the championship of Division B.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She also represented Croatia at the 2022 FIBA U16 European Championships in Portugal, averaging 13.6 points and a tournament-best 15.0 rebounds over seven games. She led Croatia to a third-place finish, including a 16-point, 13-rebound effort against Spain in the semifinals. She produced six double-doubles, including a 19-point, 15-rebound effort in a win over Italy, and a huge 14-point, 23-rebound performance in a win over Finland. She also averaged 2.4 blocks and 1.7 steals.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The daughter of Darko and Stanka Bozan, Petra also played club basketball for WBC Akademija Zana Lelas. A finance major, Bozan has earned three spots on the Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll. She followed with two rebounds and an assist in NU's 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Neale tipped her Husker career with a five-point effort in 10 minutes off the bench in a 104-40 exhibition win over Mount Marty (Oct. 24).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"We are beyond excited to make things official with the signing of Alanna Neale,\" Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said. \"She joins us from one of the winningest and most successful high school programs in the country and is coming off a stellar senior season. We have seen Alanna use her skillset to impact the game on both sides of the ball and as a rebounding guard. There is so much excitement knowing that her best basketball is still in front of her. We can't wait to get her to Lincoln.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Neale is the first player from the Los Angeles area to sign with the Huskers since Tear'a Laudermill (Moreno Valley/Canyon Springs High School) in 2011. Laudermill was a two-time All-Big Ten selection and ranks among the top-25 players in scoring all-time at Nebraska. She was a member of four NCAA Tournament teams and part of the most successful four-year span in school history.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Neale averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.2 steals over 32 games as a senior for Ontario Christian, which entered California's Open Division state championship ranked No. 1 nationally, before falling in the semifinal to the nation's No. 6 team. The Lady Knights finished the season with a 30-2 overall record. She earned All-CIF Southern Section honors.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior in 2023-24, Neale was named the MVP of the Olympic League and a first-team all-conference pick at Village Christian High School in Sun Valley, Calif., after averaging 18.2 points, 9.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.1 steals over 25 games for the Crusaders.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Neale spent her sophomore season at Chaminade High School in West Hills, Calif., where she was a second-team All-CIF selection and a first-team All-Mission League pick. She was also rated as one of the top 15 sophomores in the CIF Southern Section. In the first round of the CIF state playoffs, Neale erupted for 21 points against Ontario Christian.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The daughter of Al and Catherine Neale, Alanna has a brother, Aj, and a sister, Aubrey. All-Tournament Team (2025)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>SoCon Player of the Week (Feb. 4, 2025)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>Kentucky Miss Basketball Finalist (2024)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>Kentucky Region 1 Player of the Year (2024)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>KHSAA All-Tournament Team (2024)\u003C/li>\n\u003C/ul>\n\u003Cp>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>The last of four transfers to join the Huskers ahead of the 2025-26 season, All-Southern Conference guard Claire Johnson signed with Nebraska on May 5, 2025.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 29 games, Johnson is averaging 3.5 points in 11 minutes per game off the bench.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Johnson led five Huskers in double figures with a game-high 21 points in 19 minutes in Nebraska's 103-46 season-opening win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3). She hit 7-of-9 shots from the field, including 2-of-3 three-pointers, while knocking down all five of her free throw attempts. She closed the first quarter with nine straight points in a 2:20 span to fuel an 18-0 run.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Johnson added 11 points, two rebounds and an assist in Nebraska's 84-50 run past Creighton (Nov. 12), before pitching in double figures for the third time this season with 10 points, two rebounds and two assists in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with nine points and two steals off the bench in Nebraska's win over Rutgers (Feb. 28), hitting her first three-pointer since Dec. 14.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Johnson pitched in eight points, including a pair of three-pointers, two rebounds and an assist in NU's 103-58 run past Oral Roberts (Nov. 19). Johnson added seven big points in a Big Ten home win over Purdue (Jan. 4). She had six points in a win over Northwestern (Jan. 28) and contributed six points and two assists in an 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>“We are thrilled to be adding Claire Johnson to the Husker women’s basketball family,\" Nebraska Coach Amy Williams said. \"Claire is coming off an outstanding freshman campaign where she showcased her versatility, efficiency and ability to impact games. Her skillset coupled with her maturity, focus and work ethic make her the perfect fit for the Huskers.”\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Johnson averaged 12.2 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals as a freshman at Samford in 2024-25. The 5-9 guard from Paducah, Ky., came on strong down the stretch for the Bulldogs, starting the team's final 14 games to earn second-team All-SoCon honors. Over the final 10 games of the season, Johnson averaged nearly 19 points while adding 2.7 assists and 1.5 steals per game. She also claimed a spot on the SoCon All-Tournament team after going for 19 points and a career-high seven rebounds in a narrow loss to Wofford (March 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Before Nebraska (Samford, 2024-25)\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>In her lone season at Samford, Johnson averaged 12.2 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists to earn second-team All-SoCon honors and a spot on the SoCon All-Tournament team. She played in 30 games with 14 starts for Samford, hitting 47.2 percent (120-174) of her shots from the field, including a sizzling 40.4 percent (61-151) of her three-pointers. She also knocked down 87.7 percent (64-73) of her free throws. She played at least 30 minutes in each of her final 11 games of the season.\u003C/p>\n\u003Cp>Johnson showed her explosiveness in midseason, earning SoCon Player-of-the-Week honors (Feb. 4) after averaging 28.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists in back-to-back games against Western Carolina and UNC Greensboro. She opened the week with a then-career-high 26 points on a then-career-high five three-pointers to go with a career-high four steals against Western Carolina (Jan. 30), before erupting for a career-high 30 points and career highs of nine made field goals and nine made free throws against UNCG (Feb. 1). \u003C/p>\n\u003Cp>In her collegiate debut, Johnson scored 13 points on 4-of-6 shooting with a pair of three-pointers to go with four rebounds in 22 minutes off the bench in a loss at Tennessee (Nov. 5). Two games later, she added 13 points and two more threes at Memphis, before scoring eight points at Florida State (Nov. 14). Later in the non-conference campaign, she added 10 points on perfect shooting (3-3 FG, 2-2 3FG, 2-2 FT) at TCU (Dec. 17).\u003C/p>\n\u003Cp>For the season, Johnson produced double figures 18 times, including nine of the last 10 games. She hit multiple three-pointers in a game 18 times, including a career-high six against Western Carolina in the regular-season finale (March 1). She also hit six threes in just 19 minutes off the bench against Berry College (Jan. 4).\u003C/p>\n\u003Cp>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Johnson committed to Samford following her junior season at McCracken County High School, where she was one of 16 finalists for Kentucky Miss Basketball honors as the Region 1 Player of the Year as a senior in 2023-24. She scored more than 2,000 points during her high school career and finished her senior season with 878 total points (23.1 ppg). She also ranked fifth in the state in free throw percentage (.844). She led the Mustangs to the 2024 KHSAA state championship game with a 39-point performance in a state semifinal win over Butler. She was a member of the 2024 KHSAA All-Tournament team. She averaged 17 points per game for McCracken County as a junior, and began playing for the Mustangs varsity team while she was still in junior high school. McCracken County went 98-10 in her final three seasons. Johnson scored 26 points in the Kentucky-Ohio All-Star game following her senior season. She was also invited to play in the Kentucky-Indiana All-Star game, but did not participate.\u003C/p>\n\u003Cp>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Michael and Ashley Johnson, Claire was born May 31, 2006. She has two brothers, Grant and Isaac. Claire earned a spot on the Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll in the fall of 2025. She was the valedictorian of her high school class. (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>\n\u003Cdiv>Emily Fisher was one of four NCAA Division I transfers to join the Nebraska women's basketball program in the spring of 2025. The Huskers announced the signing of the 6-0 guard/forward on April 16.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher, who spent her first two collegiate seasons at Maryland, comes to Lincoln after playing 52 games with the Terrapins.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She made a strong Husker debut with a career-high-tying nine points and a career-high four steals to go along with a career-high-matching three assists in a 103-46 win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3). She added four rebounds and a block for the Big Red in 20 minutes off the bench.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher produced a six-point effort in just four first-half minutes at No. 8 Michigan (Feb. 4). Fisher converted a traditional three-point play before knocking down her first three-pointer of the season late in the half to help Nebraska take a 44-42 lead to halftime. She added five points on perfect shooting in 14 minutes in her first Big Ten appearance at No. 14 Iowa (Jan. 1).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She closed the regular season with a career-high four assists to go with two points, a rebound and a block in a win over Rutgers (Feb. 28). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher had a season-high six rebounds to go with two assists, a steal and a block in eight minutes in NU's 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9). She added two points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals in 10 minutes in an 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She did not play in Nebraska's exhibition win over Mount Marty (Oct. 24) because of a minor lower leg injury suffered in practice. Fisher also missed NU's wins over Samford (Nov. 8) and Creighton (Nov. 12) with a separate lower body injury suffered in practice after the win over Northwestern State.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher returned for 90 seconds in the win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16), before getting two points and a rebound in 11 minutes of NU's 103-58 win over ORU (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She did not play in Nebraska's Emerald Coast Classic wins over Purdue Fort Wayne and Virginia (Nov. 24-25), but returned to the court for seven minutes in a win over Bradley (Dec. 3).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"We had a strong relationship with Emily from her recruitment out of high school and believe that she fits perfectly with our tough, hard-nosed, gritty, hard-working culture here at Nebraska,\" Husker Head Coach Amy Williams said. \"She brings a versatility and a willingness to guard almost any position on the floor. We are excited to have her spend her remaining two years here in Lincoln.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher played her best game of the season in Maryland's 91-71 loss to Nebraska in College Park. Fisher finished with a season-high eight points, including her first career made three-pointer. She added a season-high two assists against the Big Red.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003C/div>\n\u003C/div>\n\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2024-25, Maryland)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>As a sophomore, Fisher missed 11 games with a concussion, but averaged 1.7 points and 1.4 rebounds over 19 contests while helping the Terps to the NCAA Sweet Sixteen. In Nebraska's 91-71 regular-season win at No. 17 Maryland (Feb. 13), Fisher finished with a season-high eight points, while adding two rebounds and two assists in 27 minutes of action.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher added solid showings in conference play with four points and a season-high four rebounds against Illinois (Feb. 2), before adding four points and three rebounds in a 79-61 win at Oregon (Feb. 6).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2023-24, Maryland)\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>As a freshman at Maryland, Fisher averaged 2.6 points and 2.8 rebounds while playing in all 33 games for a Terp team that advanced to the first round of the NCAA Tournament. She scored a career-high nine points and added a career-best eight rebounds in a win over Towson (Dec. 12). She also had eight points at both Penn State (Jan. 28) and against UMass (Nov. 25). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher scored six points and grabbed eight rebounds in a career-high 29 minutes against George Mason. She also had seven points and five rebounds in a win over Wisconsin.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She opened her collegiate career with four points and four rebounds against Harvard (Nov. 6), before seeing playing time at both South Carolina (Nov. 12) and UConn (Nov. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In addition to scoring eight points against Penn State in Big Ten play, Fisher had seven points and five rebounds in 14 minutes of work in a win over Wisconsin (Feb. 29). She added five points and three rebounds at Rutgers (Feb. 21).\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>She found the scoring column in 14 of her final 15 regular-season conference games.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Fisher capped her freshman campaign with three points and two rebounds against Iowa State in the NCAA Tournament (March 22).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Fisher was ranked as the No. 80 overall prospect by ESPN out of Libertyville High School in Illinois. She averaged 13.7 points, 6.8 rebounds and 4.6 assists as a senior in 2022-23, when she was named the captain of the Lake County All-Area team. As a junior, she a was a first-team Illinois Class 4A all-state selection, the North Suburban Conference Player of the Year, and a first-team all-conference and all-area choice at Libertyville. Fisher recorded nine double-doubles, including a pair of triple-doubles as a junior. She was also Libertyville's all-time leader in blocked shots with 100. She played AAU basketball for the Wolverinas.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>The daughter of Jeramy and Renee Fisher, Emily has two younger siblings, Lily and Luke. Conference (First Team, 2022)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>Missouri Class 5 State High Jump Champion (2019, 2021)\u003C/li>\n\u003C/ul>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Senior (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Nebraska added size, experience and athleticism with the signing of Eliza Maupin (pronounced MOP-in) to its 2025-26 women's basketball roster, Husker Head Coach Amy Williams announced on Monday, April 14.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin, a 6-3 forward from Webster Groves, Mo., joined the Huskers after playing in 33 games with two starts for Kansas State as a junior in 2024-25. Maupin hit 63.2 percent (55-87) of her shots from the field while averaging 3.9 points and 2.8 rebounds per game. She also dished out a career-high 29 assists and blocked a career-best 17 shots for the Wildcats.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She notched her fifth career double-double and second as a Husker with 13 points and a career-high 13 rebounds to go with a career-high four assists, two blocks and two steals at Wisconsin (Jan. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin posted her first Husker double-double with 12 points and a then-career-high-tying 11 rebounds in her first Nebraska start at No. 14 Iowa (Jan. 1).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin, who is averaging career bests of 7.9 points and 4.4 rebounds, has produced double figures nine times this season, including 11 points and six rebounds against No. 15 Iowa (Feb. 16). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced 13 points on 4-of-5 shooting in a win over Purdue (Jan. 4). Maupin also had 10 points against No. 4 UCLA (Jan. 11), after getting nine points and seven rebounds in a win over Indiana (Jan. 8). She also had a career-high three blocks against the Hoosiers.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin put up a season-high 17 points to go with five rebounds, three assists and a block in NU's 103-58 win over Oral Roberts (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She followed with 13 points on 6-of-6 shooting to go with four rebounds and three assists in a win over Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24). She closed out Nebraska's Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship with six points, four rebounds and two steals in a win over Virginia (Nov. 25).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added 11 points and five boards in NU's 85-44 win over Illinois State (Dec. 14), before notching 10 points and four boards in the Big Ten home opener against No. 17 USC (Dec. 29).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin contributed seven points and three rebounds in NU's 92-53 win over Bradley (Dec. 3), before getting seven points, six boards and two assists in an 87-35 win over Omaha (Dec. 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin made her NU debut with five points, four rebounds and a career-high-tying two blocks in an 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12). She added eight points, three boards and two assists in a win over North Dakota State (Nov. 16). She missed NU's first two regular-season games and its exhibition win over Mount Marty (Oct. 24) because of a minor lower leg injury suffered in practice. She re-tweaked the injury prior to the opener with Northwestern State.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"We are so excited to welcome Eliza to the Husker women's basketball family,\" Williams said. \"She has a winning mindset and strong desire to develop, which fits perfectly in our culture. Her length, athleticism, skillset and experience make her primed to excel on both sides of the ball within our system.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In three seasons at KSU, Maupin played in 98 games with three starts while converting 62.3 percent (157-252) of her field goal attempts. She totaled 390 points, 263 rebounds, 47 assists, 38 blocks and 49 steals. She averaged 4.0 points and 2.7 rebounds in 11.7 minutes per game as a Wildcat.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin, who has scored in double figures 19 times, owns five career double-doubles.\n\u003Cdiv>She has been perfect from the field with at least five makes on four occasions in her career, including 7-for-7 at Texas (Feb. 4, 2024), 6-for-6 at Baylor (Jan. 22, 2024), 6-for-6 against USC Upstate (Dec. 5, 2024) and 6-for-6 as a Husker against Purdue Fort Wayne (Nov. 24, 2025).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin has appeared in three career NCAA Tournament games, scoring 11 total points on a combined 5-of-6 shooting (.833) while hitting her only free throw attempt in 18 total minutes.\u003C/div>\n\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Junior (2024-25, Kansas State)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Maupin played in 33 games with two starts as a junior for K-State, totaling 128 points, 92 rebounds and career season bests of 29 assists and 17 blocked shots. She also nabbed 13 steals. She produced a season-high 15 points on perfect shooting (6-for-6 FG, 3-for-3 FT) to go with five rebounds, three assists and three steals in a win over USC Upstate (Dec. 5). Maupin had 10 points and eight rebounds in a win over Little Rock (Nov. 18). She added nine points, seven rebounds and two assists against Eastern Illinois (Dec. 3). She also produced six points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks against Arizona State (Jan. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2023-24, Kansas State)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>As a sophomore in 2023-24, Maupin appeared in 29 games and averaged 4.0 points per game while shooting a career-best 68.7 percent (46-67) from the field. She added 2.3 rebounds per game. She notched her third career double-double with 15 points and a career-high 11 rebounds to go with three steals off the bench against UCF (Feb. 17). Maupin erupted for a career-high 18 points on 7-for-7 shooting in a career-high 30 minutes off the bench at Texas (Feb. 4). She added 16 points on 6-for-6 shooting, including her first career three-pointer, to go with nine rebounds in 29 minutes off the bench at Baylor (Jan. 22). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In Big 12 Conference play, Maupin hit an incredible 72.7 percent (32-44), including a five-game stretch midway through the conference season in which she hit 19-of-21 shots (.905) including her only career three-pointer.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>The stretch started with a 3-for-3 effort against Kansas (Jan. 20), before she went 6-for-6 with a three-pointer to finish with 16 points and nine rebounds against Baylor (Jan. 22). Maupin hit 1-of-3 shots against BYU (Jan. 27), before going 2-for-2 against Oklahoma (Jan. 31) and 7-for-7 against Texas (Feb. 4) on her way to a career-high 18 points against the Longhorns.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2022-23, Kansas State)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Maupin played in 36 games with one start as a true freshman for the Wildcats in 2022-23, averaging 4.1 points and 2.9 rebounds per game. She hit 57.1 percent of her shots from the field, while adding 15 blocked shots and 17 steals on the year.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced her first career double-double with 12 points and 10 rebounds in just 13 minutes of work in a win over Utah Tech (Nov. 20). She added her second double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds in 22 minutes at TCU (Feb. 18). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin just missed another double-double with 11 points and nine rebounds off the bench at West Virginia (Feb. 25). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She pumped in a season-high 14 points to go with five rebounds at Oklahoma (March 1) for her sixth double-figure scoring effort of her freshman campaign.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Maupin produced her final double-digit scoring performance of the season with 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting against Texas Tech at the Big 12 Tournament (March 9).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Maupin earned Missouri Class 5 All-State honors as a senior at Webster Groves High School in 2022 after averaging 15.3 points on 61 percent shooting, including 34 percent from three-point range. She added 7.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 rebounds on her way to Class 5 District 2 Player-of-the-Year honors and first-team All-Suburban Conference accolades.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>As a junior in 2021, Maupin averaged 12.3 points and 5.3 rebounds while shooting 54 percent from the field and 47 percent from three-point range to help Webster Groves to a Missouri Class 6 state runner-up finish. She was also a significant contributor for the Stateswomen as a freshman and sophomore. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In addition to her exploits on the basketball court, Maupin was the Missouri Class 5 state high jump champion as a freshman in 2019 and as a junior in 2021. & Awards\u003C/strong>\u003C/p>\n\u003Cul>\n\u003Cli>Nebraska Scholar-Athlete Honor Roll (Fall 2025)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>No. 35 Recruit Nationally by ESPN (2021)\u003C/li>\n\u003Cli>Three-Time All-Ohio Division I All-State (Second Team, 2021; Third Team, 2019, 2020)\u003C/li>\n\u003C/ul>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Graduate (2025-26)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Nebraska bolstered its 2025-26 backcourt with an experienced Big Ten guard when Husker women's basketball coach Amy Williams announced the signing of Hailey Weaver on April 14.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Through 29 games as a Husker, Weaver is averaging 2.6 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.0 assist. She put up a season-high 11 points to go with five rebounds in Nebraska's Emerald Coast Classic Beach Bracket championship game win over Virginia (Nov. 25). Weaver lifted the Huskers with 11 third-quarter points in a three-minute span, including 3-of-3 three-point shooting.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced an eight-point effort to go with three rebounds, three assists and three steals in an 87-56 win over Cal Baptist to close non-conference play (Dec. 21).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She added six points, three rebounds, three assists, a block and a steal in Nebraska's Big Ten-opening win over Penn State (Dec. 6). She also scored six points on a pair of three-pointers against No. 15 Iowa (Feb. 16).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weaver made her regular-season Husker debut as a starter with four points, two rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block in Nebraska's 103-46 win over Northwestern State (Nov. 3). She added five points, three boards, two assists and four steals in an 80-46 win over Samford (Nov. 8), before pitching in six points on her first two three-pointers as a Husker in an 84-50 win over Creighton (Nov. 12).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She had four points, two rebounds, two steals and a career-high-tying two blocks in NU's 82-70 win over North Dakota State in Sioux Falls, S.D. (Nov. 16). She had four points, a season-high eight rebounds to go with two more blocks and a steal in a 103-58 run past ORU (Nov. 19).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weaver, who spent three seasons on the court at Northwestern from 2021-22 through 2023-24 before sitting out the 2024-25 season, is a graduate student at Nebraska in 2025-26.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\"We are thrilled that Hailey will be finishing her career at Nebraska,\" Williams said. \"Her versatility on the offensive side of the ball makes her a great fit with our team and our style of play. She has three years of experience guarding in the Big Ten Conference, and we are excited for what she brings to us on that side of the ball as well.\"\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In three career games against the Huskers at Pinnacle Bank Arena, Weaver went 5-for-11 from beyond the arc. She scored 11 points on 2-of-5 long-range shooting in a loss to the Huskers in Lincoln (Feb. 20, 2024). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>In one of the best games of her sophomore season, Weaver pumped in 12 points on 2-of-5 three-pointers to go along with three steals and two assists in a setback to the Big Red at PBA (Feb. 26, 2023). She added a three-pointer in Lincoln on her only shot attempt as a freshman against the Huskers (Feb. 27, 2022).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weaver has totaled 383 points, 183 rebounds, 86 assists and 91 steals as a collegian, while going 56-of-159 (.352) from three-point range. She has produced double-figure points 15 times in her career.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She has averaged 3.8 points over 55 career Big Ten Conference regular-season games.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Redshirt (2024-25, Northwestern)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Weaver took a redshirt season and did not compete for Northwestern in 2024-25. She earned her bachelor's degree from Northwestern and is pursuing a graduate business certificate in marketing analytics from Nebraska.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Junior (2023-24, Northwestern)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Over the first seven games of her junior season, Weaver scored in double figures seven straight times capped by a career-high 20 points against Loyola-Chicago (Nov. 29). The stretch began with back-to-back 15-point games to open the season, before she notched the only double-double of her career with 12 points and a career-high 13 rebounds against Florida State (Nov. 22). During the stretch, Weaver went 16-for-30 (.520) from three-point range, including 3-for-5 from beyond the arc on her way to 11 points against Notre Dame (Nov. 15, 2023).\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She scored 11 points on 2-of-5 long-range shooting in a loss to the Huskers in Lincoln (Feb. 20). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>For the season, Weaver averaged career bests of 7.9 points and 3.1 rebounds per game, while shooting 36 percent (32-89) from three-point range and 83.8 percent (31-37) from the free throw line.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>She produced double figures in points 12 times, while starting 14 of 28 games. Weaver averaged 11.4 points and 4.2 rebounds while starting each of her first 10 games as a junior, but averaged 5.9 points and 2.4 rebounds while making just four starts over the last 18 games of the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Sophomore (2022-23, Northwestern)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Weaver's contributions increased during her second season at Northwestern. She played in 28 games for the Wildcats and averaged nearly 11 minutes per game off the bench. \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Weaver averaged 3.0 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game for the Wildcats. She erupted for a season-high 14 points on a career-best 3-of-4 three-pointers at Purdue (Feb. 12). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Two weeks later she added the second double-figure scoring effort of her college career when she pumped in 12 points on 2-of-5 three-pointers to go along with three steals and two assists in a loss at Nebraska (Feb. 26). \u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Over the last 10 regular-season games of 2022-23, Weaver averaged 5.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.9 steals in just 15.7 minutes per game, after averaging 1.8 points, 1.2 rebounds and 0.8 steals in just under eight minutes per game through the first 17 contests of the season.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>Freshman (2021-22, Northwestern)\u003Cbr>\u003C/strong>Weaver played six games during her true freshman season at Northwestern. Her sporadic contributions came in each month of the regular season, playing in two games in November, one in December, one in January and two in late February. She hit a three-pointer against Nebraska in Lincoln on her only shot attempt in one minute of play (Feb. 27). She went 3-for-3 from three-point range in Big Ten play on the road at Maryland (Jan. 23), at Illinois (Feb. 20) and at Nebraska (Feb. 27), scoring nine points in just nine total minutes over three Big Ten road games as a freshman.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>Overall on the season, she totaled 14 points and four steals in just 21 minutes, while hitting 50 percent (4-8) of her shots, including 60 percent (3-5) of her three-point tries.\u003Cbr>\u003Cbr>\u003Cstrong>High School\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>Weaver was named to the 2021 Jersey Mike's Naismith National High School Girls Trophy Watch List. She was ranked as the No. 35 overall recruit in the nation by ESPN. She was named second-team All-Ohio Division I as a senior at Solon High School after averaging 11.9 points per game as a senior. She claimed third-team All-Ohio honors as a sophomore in 2019 (15.0 ppg) and as a junior in 2020 (16.4 ppg). She was also an academic honor roll selection throughout high school. \u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv> \u003C/div>\n\u003Cdiv>\u003Cstrong>Personal\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr>The daughter of Kevin and Stephanie Weaver, Hailey also was recruited by Michigan, Marquette, Pittsburgh, Kentucky and Miami out of high school. She earned her bachelor's degree from Northwestern in 2025 and is pursuing a graduate certificate in marketing analytics from Nebraska.
